meta.title: Fix cudagraph record_stream memory leak
meta.body_summary: Fix CUDA graph memory leak when record_stream is used during capture by processing pending events at the end of allocation to the pool; includes a test for no leak.

perf_labels.notes: Codex-generated fix to process pending events in endAllocateToPool; PR closed without merge due to CI lint/label failures and maintainer desire for more review despite one approval.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 33 changed lines across 2 files (only 4 lines in CUDACachingAllocator.cpp), this is a tiny edit by absolute volume. It fits a targeted fix for a complex memory leak, but the PR was closed without merge despite one approval, indicating the small scope did not guarantee acceptance due to unresolved CI issues and maintainer caution.

review_details.concern_detail: Reviewers questioned whether the fix reduces reserved memory or just allocated memory and discussed alternative solutions like removing record_stream from the autograd engine; the provided test could not be run due to a missing psutil module.
review_details.performance_claim: Fix CUDA graph memory leak when record_stream is used during capture, allowing memory to be reclaimed after capture ends.
review_details.rejection_signals: PR closed without merge despite one approval; CI lint failure and missing labels; author indicated need for more scrutiny ('Treat this like a third party PR'), suggesting the fix was not fully trusted or complete.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Fixing a CUDA memory leak in the caching allocator during graph capture required understanding of event processing, stream semantics, and interaction with record_stream. Codex produced a small, plausible fix but could not address the broader design discussion about eliminating record_stream from autograd.

detection_detail.code_reading: Reviewers eqy and pritamdamania87 analyzed the code change in endAllocateToPool and discussed whether it addresses actual reserved memory leak or just allocated memory, referencing the allocator code.
detection_detail.ci_auto: CI flagged lint errors in test_cuda.py and missing release notes label, but no performance-related CI checks.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: Test provided but could not be executed due to missing psutil module; no benchmark or before/after memory measurements.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR closed without merging; CI failures and maintainer's request for more scrutiny indicated the fix was not considered complete.

core_change_summary.description: In c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp, added a call to process pending events at the end of endAllocateToPool to ensure that memory used by record_stream tensors during graph capture can be freed. In test/test_cuda.py, added test_graph_record_stream_no_leak that captures a graph with cross-stream operations and checks that memory allocated after capture does not increase.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Only two files changed; the allocator change is 4 lines, test adds 29 lines.
change_trajectory: Single commit: added processEvents call in endAllocateToPool and new leak test.
CI flagged lint issues and missing labels; PR discussed but not merged.

review_signals.summary: Naive question: does this decrease the total reserved memory or just the reported allocated memory?
review_signals.action_taken: Discussion ensued about the actual effect on memory.

review_signals.summary: Suggested putting the graph capture in a loop with larger allocations to demonstrate OOM; also record_stream on x in the other stream.
Pointed out that all allocator changes are in endAllocateToPool, so they only affect after capture, not during.
Argued the right fix is to get rid of record_stream in the autograd engine.
review_signals.action_taken: Led to further discussion and an experimental PR (#155857).

review_signals.summary: PR makes things strictly better even if only marginally; should land regardless of other record_stream discussions.
APPROVED stating this is making things strictly better, so why not?
Maybe get context only if you are going to use it?
Treat this like a third party PR — do not trust the fix without thorough review.
CI reported lint errors in test_cuda.py and missing release notes label.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened by ezyang with single commit from Codex.
Immediate CI bot comments about lint and labels; ezyang stated he hadn't reviewed yet.
Reviewers eqy and pritamdamania87 engaged in discussion about the fix's actual impact, alternative approaches, and test design.
ngimel approved after 5 days, but ezyang requested more scrutiny, leading to no merge.
PR closed without merge, likely due to unresolved CI issues and maintainer's lack of confidence.
